question: A material has a forbidden energy gap of $5\text{ eV}$ between its valence band and conduction band. Will it behave as a conductor or an insulator at room temperature? Give reason.

options.A: It behaves as an insulator at room temperature. A $5\text{ eV}$ forbidden gap is large, so thermal energy is insufficient to excite many electrons into the conduction band.
options.B: It behaves as a conductor because a $5\text{ eV}$ gap allows electrons to enter the conduction band easily at room temperature.
options.C: It behaves as a semiconductor because every material with a non-zero energy gap has moderate conductivity.
options.D: It behaves as a superconductor because its conduction band is completely filled.
